How will we learn which onboarding fixes work?

Long image

A

Answer

Test a flow rebuilt around the patient against today's flow, not fixes to today's steps. The lead hypothesis, H-00, reorders the whole flow; the 13 step-level hypotheses become its parts, and 3 of them ship to everyone.

  1. Today's care flow first asks why the patient is here on screen 10 of 17; 12 of its 17 screens serve insurance, payment, identity or scheduling.
  2. The portal gets about 197 sessions a day, so a 4-week test can only detect lifts of 3% to 14% relative. Small fixes are both undetectable and the wrong lever.1
  3. Bundle A, Talk first, is the lead test of H-00. Coverage (T-04) and price (T-12) are tested inside it, at its later steps.
  4. Safety screening and consent stay early and are never held back from a control group.

Applies toHypotheses v2built on Observations v2 and decision D-10 (proposed)power from PostHog portal sessions, 30 days to Aug 29, 202650/50 split, 80% power, 5% two-sided

1

What is the lead hypothesis?

H-00. A flow ordered around the patient will get more patients to a completed first visit than any set of fixes to today's steps. The order: understand the need, reassure, match with a stated reason, then insurance, payment and scheduling. Safety checks stay early, framed as care.

Where does each test sit in the funnel?

Diagram structure
  • Entry: T-01 entry
  • Account: T-02, T-03 account
  • Coverage: T-04 coverage
  • Intake: T-06, T-08 intake
  • Match: T-09, T-10 match
  • Payment: T-12 pay
  • First visit: T-13 visit
  • account → coverage
  • coverage → intake
  • entry → account
  • intake → match
  • match → pay
  • pay → visit

Every step is red: each one carries a friction point and at least one test.

  1. Entry: T-01 ↗

    H-01. "Tell us what's going on" vs. "Book Appointment Now". Measures visitors who finish intake. Needs marketing-site traffic.

  2. Account: T-02, T-03 ↗

    H-02. Account after the match vs. account first. H-03. Returning patients confirm what's on file vs. jump to providers. Need care-flow tracking.

  3. Coverage: T-04 ↗

    H-04. Member ID, live eligibility and a cost estimate vs. a logo pick. Guardrail: the insurance step (92.7% today) can't drop more than 2.6 points.

  4. Intake: T-06, T-08 ↗

    H-06. Plain-language conversation vs. diagnostic chips, 3 arms, detects 7% relative. H-08. Prefilled answers vs. asking again.

  5. Match: T-09, T-10 ↗

    H-09. Top 3 with a reason each vs. a long list; detects 8% relative on 63.4%. H-10. Dated slot, auto-booking waitlist or priced self-pay vs. "please call".

  6. Payment: T-12 ↗

    H-12. 2×2 of price breakdown × one-tap wallets. Needs a payment-success event.

  7. First visit: T-13 ↗

    H-13. A "Your first visit" card before booking vs. none. Measures show rate. Needs visit tracking.

How small a lift can each step detect?

Portal sessions per day
About 197 (5,898 in 30 days)
Match to selected, today
63.4% · detectable change 5.1 points in 28 days
Fit check to conditions, 3 arms
4.6 points (7% relative) in 28 days
Rule (D-09, proposed)
Test only changes expected to move a step by 8% or more

These are sessions, not people

One person can make several sessions, so power per person is lower than shown. Re-run the numbers once person-level tracking exists.

BundleCombinesThe bet
A. Talk first (lead, tests H-00)H-01, H-02, H-06, H-07, H-08Patients heard in their own words before sign-up finish intake and trust the match.
B. Know your cost firstH-04, H-11, H-12, H-13Patients who know coverage, price and visit format early book and show up.
C. A real slot, explainedH-03, H-09, H-10, H-13A reason for each match and a guaranteed next step stop the matching drop. Needs the supply question answered.

Bundle A runs first, 50/50 per person against the current flow; B and C supply its later steps. Primary metric: first visit completed within N days (D-06).
